---- Applicant
 Versus

Amleshwar, District Durg Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent
For Applicant : Mr. Shalvik Tiwari, Advocate For Respondent : Mr. U.K.S. Chandel, Dy.A.G. For
Objector : Mr. Syed Asfaque Hussain Rizvi, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu
Order On Board 16/04/2024
1.

Applicant has filed this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 for grant of regular bail as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No.173 of 2022,
registered at Police Station - Amleshwar, District - Durg (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section
420, 467, 468, 201, 294 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.

2.  Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 16.11.2022 complainant Narendra Kumar Deshlahre lodged a report to the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:13730 concerned police station stating that applicant along with other co-accused persons have allured him that they will provide Government job to him and in lieu thereof he is required to pay Rs.35 lakhs upon which he paid Rs.35 lakhs to the accused persons, however, he was not provided the job.

During investigation, the police revealed that applicant along with other accused persons have taken money from other six persons also,
alluring them to provide Government job and thereby accused persons have fraudulently procured Rs.1,81,00,000/- from the victims.
Based on said report, aforementioned crime was registered and during course of investigation, applicant and other two accused were arrested on 13.7.2022.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed any offence as alleged.
There is no documentary proof that complainant or any of the victim has transferred any amount in the account of applicant.
Allegation is only oral that applicant was handed over money by complainant and other victim.
The other co-accused persons Gajendra Lahre, Purnima Lahre and Yashwant Lahre were granted bail.
Applicant is in jail since 13.07.2023.
Hence, he may be enlarged on bail.

4. Learned State counsel opposes the submission of learned counsel for applicant and would submit that applicant has taken money from as many as 8 victims giving false assurance of Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:13730 providing government job to them.

He also contended that there are documents showing that complainant/victim has procured money from Bank through loan, withdraw cash amount from their account which they received from different source, which shows that complainant/victim are having amount which is alleged to have been paid to applicant.
Other co-accused persons, who have been granted bail is on different ground as there is no allegation that the amount has been handed over to those applicants.
5. Learned counsel for Objector adopting the submission of learned State counsel opposes the submission of learned counsel for applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

7. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation, in particular the material available in the case diary stating that all the amount has been handed over to the present applicant to the tune of Rs.1,81,00,000/- giving false assurance to the complainant/victim for providing them government job, further considering that first bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn and as of now there is no change of circumstances, I do not find present to be a fit case to enlarge the applicant on regular bail at this stage.
8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:13730 Cr.P.C. is rejected.
However, the learned trial Court is directed to conclude the trial expeditiously.
